description: A vector produced by a model so that similar content ends up close together.
The dot product divided by both lengths: compares direction only, from -1 to 1; equals the dot product for normalized vectors.
Compares the query with every vector, `O(N·d)` per query: perfect recall, cost that grows with the collection.
The share of the true top `k` neighbors that an approximate index returns; the quality side of the latency trade-off.
A layered proximity graph searched greedily from a sparse top layer down; tuned with `M`, `efConstruction` and `efSearch`, kept in memory.
k-means centroids split the vectors into lists (Voronoi cells); a query scans only the `nprobe` nearest lists (pgvector `lists` and `probes`).
A graph index stored on SSD with compressed vectors in memory, for collections larger than RAM on a single machine.
Storing vectors in fewer bits (scalar, product or binary codes) to cut memory, usually followed by re-ranking with the original vectors.
